title: The Siege of Vienna
description: September-October 1529. Suleiman the Magnificent's army arrives before Vienna's medieval walls. The player commands the garrison of German Landsknechts and Spanish arquebusiers under Niklas Graf Salm: countermine the Ottoman sappers, repel assaults on the Carinthian Gate, and hold until autumn rains and supply failure force the Ottoman withdrawal.

anachronisms_found: FREDERICK_BARBAROSSA stands in for Niklas Graf Salm - Barbarossa died in 1190, some 340 years before the 1529 siege, and the engine offers plenty of generic or better-suited hero substitutes
SALADIN stands in for Suleiman the Magnificent - a 12th-century Ayyubid sultan used for a 16th-century Ottoman sultan; an unnamed Turkish unit or a Sultan-type hero would have avoided this
CAMEL_RIDER x5 in the Ottoman host besieging Vienna - camelry was not part of the 1529 Danube campaign and is out of region
No JANISSARY units at all, despite the text explicitly announcing 'his janissaries at his back' - the Turkish unique gunpowder unit is available in the engine and its omission is avoidable

Defender roster of KNIGHT, MAN_AT_ARMS, CROSSBOWMAN, SKIRMISHER for a garrison described as Landsknechts and Spanish arquebusiers - HAND_CANNONEER and TWO_HANDED_SWORDSMAN/TEUTONIC_KNIGHT exist and would fit 1529
Ottoman siege train of TREBUCHET, MANGONEL and SCORPION rather than any gunpowder artillery; the Ottomans of 1529 relied on light guns and mining, not classical torsion engines
Victory condition requires killing Suleiman, who was never killed and in fact survived to 1566

issues_found: Niklas Graf Salm is represented by FREDERICK_BARBAROSSA, a 12th-century Hohenstaufen emperor — four centuries out of period; a renamed generic Champion/Hand Cannoneer or Teutonic hero-less unit would have been correct.

Suleiman the Magnificent is represented by SALADIN, an Ayyubid Kurd of the 1180s — wrong dynasty, wrong culture, wrong century; the engine offers no Suleiman, so a renamed generic unit was the correct substitution.
Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so Vienna's garrison may render in Japanese or Mayan architecture and the Ottoman camp likewise; Teutons/Spanish vs Turks was available and free.

No Janissaries or Hand Cannoneers anywhere: the Ottoman assault force is CHAMPION x6 with CAMEL_RIDER x5, and the 'Spanish arquebusiers' of the text are rendered as CROSSBOWMAN x6 — the gunpowder character of 1529 is absent on both sides despite the engine shipping Hand Cannoneers and Janissaries.
CAMEL_RIDER on the Danube plain is a desert-theatre unit; Sipahi light cavalry and cavalry archers already cover the Ottoman horse.
1756 TREE_OAK on a 144x144 map turns the Vienna glacis into dense forest; the historical siege was fought across cleared suburbs the defenders had burned down.
ROMAN_RUINS placed as scenery is anachronistic decoration for a 16th-century fortified city (Vindobona ruins were long built over).

Victory is gated on DESTROY_OBJECT on Saladin/Suleiman. Suleiman was never engaged, never led a charge, and survived until 1566; the siege ended through attrition, rain and the campaign season, so playing to win requires an event that did not happen.
The narration asserts 'Suleiman's banner falls' as the cause of the Ottoman withdrawal, inverting the actual causation the same script elsewhere states correctly (rains, supply failure).

Only 2 BOMBARD_CANNON and 1 TREBUCHET for the besiegers, while the historical Ottoman failure was precisely that the heavy siege train was left behind and mining was substituted — the mining is narrated but modelled only as a single VILLAGER_MALE to kill.
All three defeat triggers fire DECLARE_VICTORY, so losing Salm or the Town Center awards the player a win.

SALADIN is placed as Suleiman the Magnificent: a 12th-century Kurdish/Ayyubid sultan standing in for a 16th-century Ottoman, an unrelated era and dynasty. The engine offers renameable generics (Janissary, Champion, Elite Janissary in the Turkish roster) that would have been correct.
FREDERICK_BARBAROSSA stands in for Niklas Graf Salm - a Hohenstaufen emperor of the 1180s substituted for a 1529 Landsknecht commander; a renamed Two-Handed Swordsman or Champion was available.
Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so the architecture, unit lines and language of the Ottoman besiegers and the Imperial garrison are arbitrary rather than Turkish/Teutonic-Spanish.
No gunpowder infantry anywhere: the brief's Spanish arquebusiers are represented by CROSSBOWMAN and SKIRMISHER although HAND_CANNONEER exists in the engine.

The defenders are given 2 BOMBARD_CANNON and 4 KNIGHT while the Ottomans get only a TREBUCHET and MANGONEL - inverting the actual artillery situation and adding a knightly cavalry arm the Vienna garrison did not field.
CAMEL_RIDER x5 in the Ottoman siege lines is an Egyptian/Levantine flavour unit with no place before Vienna in 1529.

The narration and victory trigger assert that Suleiman personally led the final charge and was killed ('Suleiman's banner falls') - he was never at the breach and withdrew alive to reign another 37 years.
Victory is keyed to killing the sultan, whereas the historical garrison had only to survive until the campaign season closed; the encoded goal is a decapitation raid, not a hold.
The 'Salm Falls' defeat text has him mortally wounded on the ramparts, which conflates his March 1530 death from wounds with an immediate collapse of the garrison.
